Rashi on Niddah 63b:10:1.english: Within the fixed periods - [The mishna] is speaking of bodily fixed periods.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:11:1.english: Even days and hours - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:11:2.hebrew: אינה אסורה אלא עם הנץ החמה - וכל הלילה משמשת, ואם עבר הנץ החמה ולא ראתה, משמשת כל היום. ורבי יוסי קתני לה, דדייק שעת הוסתות ותו לא:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:11:2.english: She is prohibited only at sunrise - And she may engage in marital relations the entire night; and if sunrise passed and she did not see [blood], she may engage in marital relations the entire day. And Rabbi Yosei taught this, for he is precise about the hour of the fixed periods and nothing more.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:11:3.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר כל היום שלה - מותרת לשמש משעבר הנץ החמה ולא ראתה, אבל כל הלילה שלפני הנץ החמה של וסתה אסורה לשמש. ומפרש בגמרא, דהאי למודה עם הנץ החמה דקתני - דרגילה למחזי בסוף ליליא מקמי דלימטי תחלת יממא, ואנן אסרינן לה כל עונת וסתה. נמצאת אסורה כל הלילה, שהיא עונת וסתה, ורבי יהודה מחמיר:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:11:3.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: The entire day is hers - She is permitted to engage in marital relations once sunrise has passed and she did not see [blood], but the entire night before the sunrise of her fixed cycle, she is prohibited from engaging in marital relations. And the Gemara explains that this [phrase], 'she was accustomed [to see blood] at sunrise,' which is taught [in the mishna, refers to a case] where she is accustomed to see [blood] at the end of the night, before the beginning of the day arrives; and we prohibit her [from relations for] the entire *onah* [period] of her fixed cycle. Consequently, she is prohibited the entire night, which is the *onah* of her fixed cycle, and Rabbi Yehuda is [being] stringent.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:12:1.hebrew: אסורה לשמש כל היום כולו דברי רבי יהודה - ורבי יהודה לטעמיה, דאמר: כל עונת וסתה אסורה, ועונה הוי או יום או לילה. ומי שוסתה בלילה, ואפילו בסופה, אסורה כל הלילה; ואם וסתה ביום, ואפי' בסופו, כל היום אסורה:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:12:1.english: She is prohibited from engaging in intercourse for the entire day; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda - And Rabbi Yehuda [follows] his reasoning, for he said that the entire period of her expected menstruation is prohibited, and a period is either day or night. And one whose expected menstruation is at night, even at its end, is prohibited the entire night; and if her expected menstruation is during the day, even at its end, she is prohibited the entire day.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:12:2.hebrew: עד שש שעות - דשעות דייקינן, הואיל ווסתה בשעה ששית, אינה אסורה לא לפניה ולא לאחריה:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:12:2.english: Until six hours - For we are precise about the hours: since her fixed period is in the sixth hour, she is forbidden neither before it nor after it.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:12:3.hebrew: וחוששת לשש שעות - שעה ששית היא אסורה, שהוא וסתה:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:12:3.english: And she is concerned for six hours - During the sixth hour she is forbidden, as that is her fixed cycle.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:13:1.hebrew: מן המנחה - היינו משש שעות ולמעלה, מכי ינטו צללי ערב, ובשבע כבר נטו הצללים, שהחמה במערב:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:13:1.english: From minḥa - That is, from six hours and onward, from when the shadows of evening incline; and in the seventh [hour], the shadows have already inclined, for the sun is in the west.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:17:1.hebrew: עם הנץ דמתניתין - בסוף לילה, לפיכך כל היום שלה והלילה אסורה. עם הנץ דברייתא בתחלת יממא, ולפיכך לילה מותרת ויום אסורה:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:17:1.english: "With sunrise" of the mishna - [Is] at the end of the night; therefore, the entire day is hers, and the night is prohibited. [The case of] "with sunrise" of the baraita is at the beginning of the day; and therefore, the night is permitted, and the day is prohibited.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:18:1.english: And you shall separate the children of Israel - And juxtaposed to it is: "And of her that is sick in her menstrual impurity" [Leviticus 15:33].

Rashi on Niddah 63b:19:1.hebrew: עונה אחריתי - דאם וסתה ביום, אסורה כל היום וכל הלילה שלפניו, ורבי יהודה לא אסר אלא עונת וסתה:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:19:1.english: An additional period - For if her fixed time is during the day, she is forbidden [to her husband] the entire day and the entire night preceding it, whereas Rabbi Yehuda forbade only the period of her fixed time.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:1:1.hebrew: בשופעת דם טמא מתוך דם טהור - רגילה לראות דם טהור תחלה ואח"כ דם טמא, הוי וסת, וכל שעה שתראה דם טמא אחר דם טהור, אמרינן דדיה שעתה:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:1:1.english: Where she discharges impure blood from within pure blood - [If] she is accustomed to seeing pure blood first and afterwards impure blood, this is a fixed period [veset], and whenever she sees impure blood after pure blood, we say that her time is sufficient.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:20:1.english: And why did he need two - [Why was it necessary] for Rava to teach us [both]?

Rashi on Niddah 63b:23:1.hebrew: ואינה מטהרת מן הוסת - דאסורה כל ימי וסתה, שמא תראה:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:23:1.english: And she is not purified from the fixed cycle - For she is forbidden [to her husband] all the days of her fixed cycle, lest she see [blood].

Rashi on Niddah 63b:2:1.english: Yawns - [In Old French:] baillier, meaning to yawn.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:3:1.hebrew: הרי אמרו - לקמן בשמעתין: אינה צריכה לא לשנות ולא לשלש, ומפרש לה: לשנות בוסתות כו':
Rashi on Niddah 63b:3:1.english: Behold, they said - Later in our sugya [it is stated]: "She does not need to repeat [a second time] or to repeat a third time," and [the Gemara] explains it: "To repeat" refers to [symptom-based] cycles, etc.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:3:2.hebrew: לימים שנים - וסתות דיומי, משקבעתן שתי פעמים הוי וסת:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:3:2.english: For days, two - Fixed periods of days: once she has established them two times, it is a fixed period.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:3:3.hebrew: לוסתות - דגופה, כגון הני דמתניתין, משקבעתן פעם אחת הוי וסת:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:3:3.english: For fixed cycles - [Fixed cycles] of the body, such as those [mentioned] in our mishna: once she has established them one time, it is a fixed cycle.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:3:4.hebrew: למה שלא מנו חכמים - וסת שלש. וקמיבעיא ליה לשמואל: למה שלא מנו חכמים מאי היא? והכי קאמר שמואל: אני שמעתי כן: למה שלא מנו חכמים שלש, אבל איני יודע מהו:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:3:4.english: For that which the Sages did not enumerate - [To establish] a fixed period, three [times are required]. And Shmuel was in doubt: What is "that which the Sages did not enumerate"? And this is what Shmuel is saying: "I heard thus: 'For that which the Sages did not enumerate, three [times],' but I do not know what it is."

Rashi on Niddah 63b:4:1.hebrew: מתניתין היא - דקתני וכן כיוצא בהן, ופירשה רבה בר עולא לאתויי הני:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:4:1.english: It is the mishna - As [the mishna] teaches: "And likewise anything similar to them," and Rabba bar Ulla explained it to include these.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:5:1.hebrew: הא שמעתתא - דשמואל דאמר: לימים שנים, לוסתות אחד:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:5:1.english: This tradition - That of Shmuel, who said: For days, two; for set periods, one.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:6:1.hebrew: זה וזה - כשיגיע עוד חמשה עשר, אסורה לשמש, שמא תחזור לוסתה; וכשיגיע יום עשרים נמי תאסר, שמא מעכשיו תקבע וסת ליום עשרים:
Rashi on Niddah 63b:6:1.english: This and that - When the fifteenth [day] arrives again, she is forbidden to engage in marital relations, lest she return to her fixed cycle; and when the twentieth day arrives, she is also forbidden, lest from now on she establish a fixed cycle for the twentieth day.

Rashi on Niddah 63b:7:1.hebrew: שאמר משום רבן שמעון בן גמליאל - דלא הוי חזקה בציר מתלת זימני, כדשמעינן ליה לרבן שמעון בן גמליאל בכל דוכתי: לשלישי תנשא, לרביעי לא תנשא (יבמות דף סד:):
Rashi on Niddah 63b:7:1.english: Who said [it] in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel - For a presumption is not [established] with fewer than three times, as we have heard from Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel everywhere: "To a third [husband] she may be married, [but] to a fourth she may not be married" (Yevamot 64b).

Rashi on Niddah 63b:9:1.english: And let us say: This is the statement of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel - For it is established for us in all places that he requires three times for [establishing] a presumption.

Tosafot on Niddah 63b:12:1.hebrew: אסורה לשמש כל שש שעות דברי רבי יהודה - לר' יהודה הוה שייך למתני כל היום כולו, כדמוכח בסיפא שהוא אוסר כל היום; אלא משום רבי יוסי תני לה בתרתי בבי:
Tosafot on Niddah 63b:12:1.english: She is prohibited from engaging in intercourse for all six hours, [this is] the statement of Rabbi Yehuda - According to Rabbi Yehuda, it would have been appropriate to teach "the entire day," as is evident from the latter clause, for he prohibits [intercourse] the entire day; rather, on account of Rabbi Yosei, [the Tanna] taught it in two clauses.

Tosafot on Niddah 63b:12:2.english: And she is concerned at six hours - That is, the entire sixth hour.

Tosafot on Niddah 63b:13:1.hebrew: מן המנחה ולמעלה - פירש"י: סוף שש, שמאז נוטי' צללי ערב. ופי' רשב"ם, דאף על גב דאמר בתמיד נשחט (פסחים נח.) דזמן המנחה לכל המוקדם הוי מששה שעות ומחצה ואילך, היינו משום דלא קים לן שפיר בשיעור שעות היום, אבל מן הדין הוא מתחילת ז'; ומיהו לגבי וסת נמי אסורה עד חצי שעה שביעית, דהיינו מן המנחה ולמעלה:
Tosafot on Niddah 63b:13:1.english: From minḥa onward - Rashi explained: The end of six [hours], for from then on the shadows of evening lengthen. And Rashbam explained that although it says in [the chapter] Tamid Nishḥat (Pesachim 58a) that the time of minḥa at the earliest is from six and a half hours and onward, that is because we are not well versed in [determining] the measurement of the hours of the day, but strictly by law it is from the beginning of the seventh [hour]; however, regarding a veset as well, she is forbidden until half of the seventh hour, which is [what is meant by] "from minḥa onward."

Tosafot on Niddah 63b:3:1.hebrew: לימים שנים - היינו כרבי, דאמר: בתרי זימני הויא חזקה. ושלא מנו חכמים ג' — הואיל ואינו וסת גמור, מודה רבי דבעי ג' זימני, והכי קים ליה:
Tosafot on Niddah 63b:3:1.english: At intervals of two days - This is in accordance with Rabbi, who says that with two times a presumption is established. And [as for] that which the Sages did not enumerate, [namely] three [days] — since it is not a full fixed period (veset), Rabbi concedes that it requires three times, and so he held.

Tosafot on Niddah 63b:4:1.hebrew: אכלה שום וראתה - הואיל ועל ידי מעשה הם, אינו וסת גמור ולא הוה בכלל דמתני'. וא"ת: ואמאי לא קאמר נמי קפצה וראתה, דהוו נמי על ידי מעשה? ויש לומר: דאינה קובעת וסת לקפיצות לחודיהו, כדאמר בפרק קמא (לעיל נדה יא.), דכל שתקבענה מחמת אונס, אפי' כמה פעמים לא קבעה; אבל אכלה שום לא חשיב אונס כמו טורח של קפיצה, שאין הראייה באה על ידי טורח אלא ממילא:
Tosafot on Niddah 63b:4:1.english: She ate garlic and saw [blood] - Since they are [brought about] by means of an action, it is not a full-fledged fixed period (veset), and was not included in our mishna. And if you will say: Why does [the Gemara] not also say, "She jumped and saw [blood]," which is also [brought about] by means of an action? And one can say that she does not establish a fixed period (veset) for jumping alone, as [the Gemara] says in the first chapter (above, Niddah 11a), that any [woman] who would establish [a fixed period] due to an external cause (ones), even multiple times, has not established [it]; but eating garlic is not considered an external cause (ones) like the exertion of jumping, for the bleeding does not come about through exertion, but on its own.

Tosafot on Niddah 63b:7:1.hebrew: זו דברי רשב"ג אבל חכמים אומרים כו' - לכאורה משמע זו ולא סבירא ליה, מדלא קאמר אבל רבי אומר. ואפילו את"ל הכי, לא תקשי לקמן גבי דילוג דמוקמינן שמואל כרשב"ג, דאליבא דמתניתין פליגי רב ושמואל. ולמאי דאמר מעיקרא הש"ס דפליגי בפלוגתא דרבי ורשב"ג, צריך לומר זו וסבירא ליה, כדמשני בפרק שור שנגח (ב"ק דף לז:):
Tosafot on Niddah 63b:7:1.english: This is the statement of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, but the Sages say, etc. - On the face of it, [this] implies: "This [is the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel]," and he [Shmuel] does not hold in accordance with him (zo ve-lo sevira lei), since he did not say, "but Rabbi says." And even if you say so, it is not difficult from later regarding skipping (dilug), where we establish Shmuel in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, for Rav and Shmuel disagree according to the Mishnah. And according to what the Gemara said initially, that they disagree in the dispute of Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, one must say: "This," and he holds in accordance with him (zo ve-sevira lei), as [the Gemara] resolves in the chapter [entitled] "Shor SheNagach" (Bava Kamma 37b).
